title: An Essay Towards Solving a Problem in the Doctrine of Chances
significance: Introduces inverse probability and Bayes’ Theorem, establishing the foundation of probabilistic reasoning and Bayesian statistical learning.
pull_quote: Given the number of times on which an unknown event has happened and failed: Required the chance that the probability of its happening in a single trial lies somewhere between any two degrees of probability that can be named.

title: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
significance: Foundational treatise creating information theory, mathematically defining entropy, channel capacity, and discrete information quantification.
pull_quote: The fundamental problem of communication is that of reproducing at one point either exactly or approximately a message selected at another point. Frequently the messages have meaning... these semantic aspects of communication are irrelevant to the engineering problem.

title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence
significance: Introduces the Imitation Game (Turing Test) and articulates the fundamental philosophy, arguments, and prospect of artificial machine intelligence.
pull_quote: I propose to consider the question, "Can machines think?" ... We can only see a short distance ahead, but we can see plenty there that needs to be done.

title: Learning Representations by Back-propagating Errors
authors: David Rumelhart and Geoffrey Hinton and Ronald Williams
significance: Demonstrates generalized backpropagation for multi-layer neural networks, solving the non-linear representation problem and catalyzing connectionism.
pull_quote: The representation of concepts by patterns of activity over many units allows the network to generalize to new cases in a natural way... and generalized backpropagation provides the credit-assignment mechanism required to learn internal representations.

title: Long Short-Term Memory
significance: Invents the constant error carousel and gating mechanism to eliminate vanishing gradients in recurrent networks, enabling long-range sequence modeling.
pull_quote: A novel recurrent network architecture, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), solves the vanishing gradient problem by enforcing constant error flow through constant error carousels within special units.

title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
authors: Alex Krizhevsky and Ilya Sutskever and Geoffrey Hinton
significance: Wins ImageNet 2012 by an unprecedented margin using deep convolutional networks on GPUs with ReLU and dropout, sparking modern deep learning.
pull_quote: We trained a large, deep convolutional neural network on GPUs with ReLU non-linearities and dropout, achieving top-5 error rates of 17.0%, dramatically improving upon the state of the art.

title: Attention Is All You Need
significance: Dispenses with recurrence and convolutions entirely, introducing multi-head self-attention that became the universal backbone for modern foundation models.
pull_quote: We propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output... Attention is all you need.

title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
significance: Demonstrates that massive scaling of autoregressive Transformers produces emergent few-shot learning and in-context task execution without gradient updates.
pull_quote: Scaling up language models greatly improves task-agnostic, few-shot performance, demonstrating that massive autoregressive pretraining allows models to execute diverse tasks with zero gradient updates.

title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
significance: Synergizes verbal reasoning traces with external tool actions, establishing the foundational architecture for autonomous language model agents.
pull_quote: While reasoning traces help models induce, track, and update action plans, action execution interfaces with external knowledge sources. Synergizing reasoning and acting creates agents that think, act, and observe in closed loops.

title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
significance: Demonstrates large-scale pure reinforcement learning without supervised cold-start data to elicit emergent deep reasoning and self-verification in LLMs.
pull_quote: Large-scale reinforcement learning applied directly to base models without supervised cold-start data demonstrates that reasoning capabilities naturally emerge through autonomous exploration, self-verification, and reward incentives.
